spec.title: Config and schema: the two files, variables, validation and hot reload

item.title: The keys the other domains add

spec.purpose: Every tunable is a key in one JSON file with a schema beside it; the executor's verb table is a second file. The loader resolves variables, refuses a missing or unknown key by name, validates at start, and reloads the tables.

section.title: What the config domain decides

node.title: scheduler/config/scheduler.json and executor.json: every tunable of the scheduler and the verb table of the executor, validated by the schemas beside them, variables resolved at load, the state root by variable, no default in Go

section.text: In: the two files and the tables they name. Out: one typed configuration value every domain reads, and a reload signal with the new table versions. The repository lint validates the files against their schemas.
This spec is the one registry of scheduler keys. A domain spec that needs a tunable names its key here; a key used in Go and absent from this registry is a defect of the build ticket that added it.

section.title: The files
section.text: scheduler.json in the scheduler's config directory, with scheduler.schema.json beside it: the scheduler's own settings, the keys each domain adds, and the paths of the tables it reads.
executor.json with executor.schema.json beside it: the socket, the host paths, the seat the record verb writes as, the record writer, and the verb table.
The tables stay where they are and keep their schemas: routes, policies, the flow gates, the role files. The scheduler reads them by the paths its own file names and never carries a copy.
The repository lint validates every config file that has a schema beside it, so the two new files are covered by the existing step with no lint change.

The interim bash line reads its own files (flow, runner, board, leases) until the cut-over. After it these keys are the only home of each value; the cut-over retires the interim copies, never merges them.

section.title: Variables
section.text: A string value may carry repo, host_repo, state_root, cache_root or ENV:NAME in the variable form; the loader resolves them after reading, and an unknown variable or an unset environment name is exit 3 naming it.

text.source: ROADMAP.md#Where runtime data lives; spec:SPEC-16#l-state; bin/state-root.sh

section.text: state_root is the one state root of the repository, from COQ_STATE; cache_root is the cache root, from COQ_CACHE. Every runtime path is a tree under one of them, never a directory of its own.
No HOME variable and no pattern under it: one state root serves every worktree and slot, so the scheduler reads no slot and no home directory, and the container mounts neither.

repo is the repository as mounted in the container, read-only; host_repo is the repository on the host, for the executor. The scheduler uses host_repo only in text run on the host, such as a playbook path.
The environment names are fixed so the wrapper and the files agree: COQ_SCHED_MODE for mode, COQ_SCHED_REPO for repo, COQ_REPO for host_repo, COQ_STATE, COQ_CACHE, COQ_HERDR_SESSION.
COQ_STATE and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR name the same path on both sides of the mount, so a state-root path or the executor socket in a record or a log reads the same in the container and on the host.
COQ_SCHED_IMAGE_DIGEST carries the digest the wrapper resolved from the configured tag at start; the digest key reads it through the variable form, so no file ever holds a digest.
No absolute path, host name or user name inside the file: every machine-specific value comes in through a variable, so the file lifts to another host or to object storage unchanged.

section.title: No defaults, no unknown keys
section.text: A key the scheduler reads and the file lacks is exit 3 naming the key. A key the file carries and the scheduler does not know is exit 3 naming the key. Go holds no fallback value for any key.
A silent default is a literal nobody can find; the supervisor's fourteen literals were the last time this was learned.

A value the owner fixed (sixty idle seconds, three attempts, four tickets in flight) is still a key: the schema pins it with a const or a maximum, so a test can lower it and nobody can raise it by accident.

section.title: Validation at start
section.text: Shape: every key present with its type, ranges that the schema states, mode one of off, shadow, active.
Cross checks: every role has an acknowledgement window; every kind a routes row wakes a seat for has a kinds entry; poll plus the smallest start-to-close stays within the visible bound.
The state root and every tree the file names under it exist and are writable, and the records root is readable; a missing tree is exit 3 naming it, never created silently by the loader.

The three seat budgets (system, product, shared) sum to at most max_agents of the herdr config the file names; a larger sum is exit 3 naming the sum, so the machine never refuses what the config promised.
The tables are loaded and checked by their own domains at start; a failure there is exit 3 with the file, the row and the key.

The verbs the scheduler can emit are a fixed list in the executor domain; the executor's Health names the verbs its table holds, and a missing one blocks going active rather than failing at the first job.

section.title: Hot reload of the tables
section.text: The routes, policies and flow tables and the role files reload while running: each tick compares a file's size and modification time, re-reads a changed file, runs its checks, and swaps it in whole or not at all.
A changed file that fails its checks is kept out: the loaded table stays, one 500 note names the file and the reason, latched by file name until a later change loads.

scheduler.json and executor.json do not reload; a change to either is a restart of the process it configures, because the socket, the roots, the budgets and the mode are not things to swap under running jobs.
The Reload call forces the comparison now and answers with the versions loaded.

section.title: The key registry of scheduler.json
section.text: The keys image, memory and container_name are read by the wrapper with a JSON tool before any process runs, so they carry no variable; the loader knows the whole group and reports it in Status.
section.key: The file's schema version; 1.1.0 for this revision.
What the scheduler may do; a variable so the run wrapper can set it from the environment.
The scheduler's own seat name on the records it writes.
The herdr session the executor addresses; carried to the executor's configuration too.
The herdr config the budget check reads max_agents from; the scheduler never carries its own copy of the agent cap.
The repository as mounted for reading, and on the host for text run there.
The state root and the cache root; every path below is a tree under one of them.
The records tree, the state root's records directory, read in its year and month folders; replaces the array of roots.

The halt and drain flags under the run directory, the files the interim line writes too, and the shutdown grace.
Intake's keys: the tick, the first-start boundary and the seats whose records are its own.
The retry policy of a job: three attempts, pinned by the schema, backoff with jitter, then the dead letter.
Concurrency and retention.
Confirmation windows per role and re-sends.
The bound within which a stall is visible; the deadlines themselves are the per-kind start-to-close.
The heartbeat under the run directory, whose age bearings stable checks outside the line.
The executor socket under the runtime directory, the dial timeout, the health interval.
The scheduler's own socket for status, reload, drain and retry.

section.title: The keys the other domains add
section.text: Revision 1.1.0 gives every threshold a rule uses a key: a probe, an idle limit, a lease, a timing or a budget that lived in a watcher's literal or a model's judgement is now a number in this file.

section.title: B routing: the per-kind table
section.text: kinds is an object keyed by record kind; each entry is the timing of the item that kind opens. The routes table says where a record goes; this table says how long its consumer may take.
section.key: From the record's time to the consumer's output record; past it the item is a stall. Replaces the per-gate stall deadlines.
The longest the consumer may go without a sign of work (a changed screen, a record, a renewed lease) before a liveness check runs.
The attempt count a seat may reach on one item before the attempt rows escalate it.

section.title: C seats: names, the idle limit and leases
section.key: How a pane reads busy or done, and how many tail lines are read.
How long a held bring-up waits for a slot, and for a seat to appear.
An idle seat with no open item for this long is downed on the next tick; sixty, the owner's limit, pinned as a maximum.
The lease a seat holds on its item; past it the reaper releases the item and downs an orphaned seat.
The roles that stand by with no work; every other seat comes up on demand and goes at the idle limit.

section.title: F health: probe thresholds
section.text: A probe is a measurement compared with one of these keys. No key names a model, a prompt or a confidence; a model only explains a finding the code raised.
section.key: The probe tick.
A busy seat whose pane tail hash is unchanged for this many ticks fails liveness.
How long a busy seat may run before the unchanged screen counts.
An idle seat with open items for this long fails readiness.
Words that, in a pane's last lines, are a finding on the next tick without the ladder's wait.
The main processes a supervised unit may have; a second copy is a stray and a finding.
The window and count of the repeat-action fingerprint: the same action this many times inside the window is a loop, which output alone hides.
The repair ladder: the first wait, its cap, and how long probes must pass before the counters reset.

section.title: The two loops and their budgets
section.text: System and product work never mix: each loop has its own tickets in flight and its own seats, the shared tier has seats, and no loop borrows the other's spare budget.
section.key: How many tickets each loop may hold in flight; the product value is at most four by the guardrail.
The live seats each loop and the shared tier may hold; the three sum within max_agents.
The top-level epics whose tickets are system work; every other epic is product. One change here moves an epic between loops.
Lending spare budget across loops; pinned false, because isolation is the point of the two loops.

section.title: The key registry of executor.json
section.key: The file's schema version.
The unix socket path the executor listens on, under the runtime directory variable.
The repository and the state root on the host, and the session every herdr verb addresses.
The seat the record verb forces on every record it writes; the scheduler cannot override it.
The event writer the record verb runs, relative to host_repo, so the spec names no writer path and the one writer stays one.
How many lines of stdout and stderr come back in a verdict.
The verb table: argv template, timeout seconds, final exit codes, the allowed flag set for the record verb.
Environment names removed before every verb, the executor pane's own identity among them, so a herdr call never targets the executor's pane by accident.

section.title: Cases the build ticket proves

case.expected: exit 0: a file lacking one key fails with exit 3 and the key's dotted name in the error
exit 0: a file with an extra key, intake.roots among them, fails naming it

section.case: No silent extras, and the 1.0.0 keys are refused.

case.expected: exit 0: repo, host_repo, state_root, cache_root and ENV names resolve; HOME, an unknown variable or an unset name fails naming it
exit 0: a role without an ack window, a woken kind without a kinds entry, a broken visible bound and a missing state tree each fail naming the key
exit 0: a changed valid table is swapped with a new version; a changed invalid one leaves the old version in place with one note
configs: schema ok, with scheduler.json and executor.json validated against their schemas

section.case: The repository lint covers the files.

case.expected: exit 0: image, memory or container_name carrying a variable form fails naming it; the digest key resolves from the environment and the group appears in Status
exit 0: seat budgets summing above max_agents fail naming the sum; borrow true fails naming the key
exit 0: idle_down_seconds above 60, retry.max_attempts above 3 and process_count other than 1 each fail naming the key; lower values load

example.text: records_root is the state_root variable followed by the records directory; the run wrapper mounts the state root read-write and the repository read-only, and nothing else.
An operator adds a routes row and saves; the next tick loads it, the log says routes loaded with the new hash, and the next record uses it.
A merger's pane ends with the word blocked; probe.blocked_words matches on the next tick and the finding goes to the maintenance lane with the evidence lines.
example.why: The probe is code against a key; nobody asked a model whether the seat was fine.

example.text: poll := cfg.PollSeconds; if poll == 0 then poll = 10.
example.why: A default nobody can find; the key is required or the file is wrong.

example.text: intake.roots listing the repository's events tree and a pattern over every treehouse slot under the home directory.
example.why: One state root serves every slot; a second root is the copying the state root replaced.

example.text: The system loop at its seat budget seats a tester from the product loop's spare budget.
example.why: No borrowing: more capacity is an owner card that raises max_agents and a budget.
